clue.text: Crotchety sleeper perhaps welcoming kip

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sleeper is a spy planted to lie dormant, so it is an example of a spy
kip is British slang for a short sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: A grumpy person who has been woken from their nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeper' tempts you towards railway sleepers or dozers; here it is an undercover agent waiting to be activated.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can describe someone irritable and quick to bark at people, the same temper as crotchety.

clue.text: As cider's drunk, making cocktails

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: As cider is drunk, cocktails get made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as the drinking of cider but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Lack of muscles means crew regularly lost

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

indicators.note: regularly lost means every other letter of the words is dropped, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is weakened by a lack of muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping alternate letters of MEANS CREW leaves E, N, C, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of something is the lack or want of it.

clue.text: Academic expert following fuel company heading for renewables

parts.note: a pro is an expert, a professional
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Esso is a petrol brand

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of renewables

explanation.surface: An academic expert advises an oil company on the move towards renewables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a link meaning after; it is the abbreviation F.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is a senior university teacher, an academic of the highest rank.

clue.text: Bang on about retired cleric

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone praises the accuracy of a remark made about a retired clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like it describes the cleric but turns CA back to AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is British slang for exactly correct, which is what accurate means.

clue.text: Rate main social works for Browning

indicators.note: works means operates on or manipulates, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Rating the main social works of the poet Robert Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like the Victorian poet but is the cooking process.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar under heat, as in cooking onions.

clue.text: Short of a French wine to serve up

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in a down clue serve up means the word for wine is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: red is red wine

explanation.surface: Someone lacks a French wine to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Under means less than, so being under a figure is falling short of it.

clue.text: Axe having a second-rate shine, needing head scrubbed

parts.note: B is a second-class grade

indicators.note: head scrubbed means the first letter is wiped away

parts.note: polish is shine on a surface

explanation.surface: An axe that has a dull shine needs its head cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like the tool with a head to scrub; it is the verb, to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a scheme is to scrap it, which is what abolish means.

clue.text: Elaborate finishes on the onyx container with diamonds

indicators.note: finishes on points to the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a pan is a cooking container
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes the finish on an onyx box set with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' looks like an adjective for an ornate box; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on a point is to expand on it, developing it in more detail.

clue.text: Cross after draw in card game

indicators.note: after says the word for cross comes after the word for draw in

parts.note: to contract is to draw in, shrink
to bridge a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry after a draw at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry and 'draw' like a tied game; both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard form of bridge, a card game for four players.

clue.text: Plate on half of armour showing stain

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: half of points to the second half of the word armour, its last three letters

explanation.surface: A knight's plate armour shows a mark of shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' sounds like armour plating, but it is a dish; OUR is the back half of ARMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonour is a stain on one's reputation, a disgrace.

clue.text: Daughter sent back inferior sink

indicators.note: sent back means the word for inferior is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: poor means inferior in quality

explanation.surface: A daughter returns a shoddy kitchen sink to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like a noun for a kitchen fitting; it is the verb, as in spirits sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or sink downwards, as flowers or spirits do.

clue.text: Setting competition with ten entered for Sweden

indicators.note: entered for means one letter goes in where another stood, replacing it

parts.note: a contest is a competition
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A contest with ten entrants put in for Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entered for' swaps the S of CONTEST for X.
explanation.definitionFit: The context of something is its setting, the surrounding circumstances.

clue.text: Bird collecting article from another planet

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the bird's name holds the article inside it

parts.note: a martin is a small bird of the swallow family
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bird picks up something from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martian is an inhabitant of Mars, a being from a planet other than Earth.

clue.text: Rook with slippery fish totters

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
eels are famously slippery fish

explanation.surface: A rook, fed slippery fish, staggers about.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger unsteadily, so reels and totters are synonyms.

clue.text: Presumably nothing left in safe

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, ... means everything on the right, so nothing on the left

explanation.surface: Someone checks a safe and finds it apparently emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase literally: if all is right, none is left.
explanation.definitionFit: All right is everyday English for unhurt, out of danger, okay.

clue.text: False one, screen in plastic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheap fake made with a plastic screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' reads as the material of the screen, but it signals that the letters are reshaped, here into NSINCERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere means not genuine, putting on feelings one lacks, hence false.

clue.text: Calm down relative consuming drink both ends of day

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the relative holds the rest inside

parts.note: a son is a relative
tea is a drink

indicators.note: both ends of points to the first and last letters of day

explanation.surface: A relative tells someone to calm down as they drink all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady on is a British exclamation telling someone to calm down or not go too far.

clue.text: Oscar received by actress cast as philosopher

indicators.note: received by means the letter is taken in by the other letters, placed inside them
cast means moulded into a new shape, so the letters of actress are rearranged

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winning actress cast in the role of a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a film role but signals the anagram: ACTRESS becomes SCRATES, with O placed after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian philosopher, teacher of Plato.

clue.text: Prevent bad smell coming up through hollow tube

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour
via means through, by way of

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, so just the outer letters of tube remain

explanation.surface: A foul smell rises up through an empty pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate a difficulty is to remove or prevent it in advance.

clue.text: Budge seal restricting opening of noodles

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the first word holds the letter penned inside it

parts.note: to seal something is to shut it

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of noodles

explanation.surface: A seal is coaxed to move by a noodle offered at its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' wants to be the animal; it is the verb, shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To shunt something is to push or shove it aside, so it is made to budge.

clue.text: Social climber put off hosting celebrity

indicators.note: hosting means entertaining a guest within, so one piece goes inside the other
off means wrong or awry, so the letters of put are rearranged

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A social climber is annoyed at having to host a famous guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as displeased; 'off' alone is the anagram signal, making UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who acts above their station, a social climber.

clue.text: Third of zoos with permits for young birds

indicators.note: Third of points to the third letter of zoos

parts.note: lets means permits, allows

explanation.surface: A third of zoos have licences to keep young birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third of' sounds like a fraction but means the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Owlets are young owls, so they are young birds.

clue.text: One's uncertain state after whiskey? I'm uncertain!

indicators.note: after says the word for state comes after the letter for whiskey

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to aver is to state firmly
er is the sound someone makes when hesitant or unsure

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy after whiskey cannot make up their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A waverer is a person who hesitates and cannot decide, someone who is uncertain.

clue.text: Measured temperature in beloved person rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
in means placed inside, so the temperature letter sits within the word for beloved person

parts.note: a dear is a beloved person

explanation.surface: Someone takes the temperature of a loved one with a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside DEAR as DETAR, which 'rising' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated means assessed or valued, as something measured against a standard.

clue.text: Fan making return visit had totally uncovered country

indicators.note: making return means the word for fan is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: totally uncovered means both words lose their outer letters, their covers

explanation.surface: An enthusiast paid a return visit to a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totally' extends the stripping to both words, not just the nearer one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Praise and kiss a soldier on base

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the kiss, a and soldier follow the base

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
X is a written kiss
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: Someone praises and kisses a soldier stationed at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' suggests a barracks; it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to glorify or praise them highly.

clue.text: Camel roamed dry ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reformed in a new order

explanation.surface: A camel wandered over arid terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun for terrain but is the anagram signal on ROAMED DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dromedary is the one-humped Arabian camel.

clue.text: Reviewed religious subject is to include earnest faster

indicators.note: re-viewed, seen again the other way, so the whole construction is read backwards

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

indicators.note: to include means the word is holds the next word inside it

parts.note: deep can mean serious or earnest, as in deep conversation

explanation.surface: A school subject is revised at a quicker pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' is read as re-viewed, looked at backwards, and turns the whole of REIDEEPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedier is the comparative of speedy, meaning quicker, so it is a synonym of faster.

clue.text: Church official taking characters from Essex to Norfolk

indicators.note: taking characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A church official travels between two English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'taking' in the definition; it belongs to the indicator, as 'Church official taking' does not define anything. Essex and Norfolk are neighbouring English counties.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church caretaker who looks after the building and churchyard.
